title: Ganesh loves the laddus, check the stock
image: The plate of laddus before Ganesh, a little emptier each time the family walks past.
scene: Day three of the festival and the plate is nearly bare. Nobody noticed, nobody said, and the sweet shop closes early this week. In the owner's godown the same thing happens with packing tape, labels and the one bearing every machine needs.
line: The laddus ran low on day three and nobody said so. The job stopped for want of a small thing. The stock colour sheet turns amber before the plate is empty, and the reorder note goes out that day.

title: Ganesh first, then the work begins
image: Before any new work begins, Ganesh is invoked first; the first step is never skipped.
scene: A new order lands at 11 am. The owner tells the floor supervisor on the phone, the supervisor tells two people in passing, and by evening nobody is sure who took the first step.
line: A new order was told to three people in passing. By evening nobody knew whose step it was. In the step-by-step job flow, every job begins with step one written against a name.

title: The scribe who never set the pen down
image: Ganesh as the scribe of the Mahabharata, writing every line as it was spoken, without a pause.
scene: The owner changed the delivery terms with a client on a call on Tuesday. By Thursday the dispatch team is still working to the old terms, because the change lived in one phone call.
line: The terms changed on a call and nobody wrote it down. Two days of work went the old way. The change record writes it the moment it is decided, where the whole team reads it.

title: The obstacle is sitting with your transporter
image: Ganesh, remover of obstacles, is asked first because something always stands in the way.
scene: The order is packed and ready. The obstacle is not in the firm at all; it is the transporter who has not confirmed the vehicle, and the owner is the one calling him for the third time.
line: The order was ready; the transporter was not. The owner spent the afternoon chasing a man outside the firm. Partner follow-up keeps that chase on a list with a date, not in the owner's phone.

title: Ten days, then the send-off
image: The idol arrives on the first day and is sent off on the tenth; everyone knows the last day before the first.
scene: A client's installation job has a start but no agreed last day. It drifts into its fourth week and the client asks the owner, not the team, when it will finish.
line: The job had a start and no end, so it ran into its fourth week. The client asked the owner for the date. Project milestones give every long job its tenth day, agreed before the first.

title: The pandal list: who brings what
image: The pandal committee's list on the wall: the lights, the flowers, the prasad, the sound, each against a name.
scene: On the pandal's wall every job has a name and a day. In the owner's office the day's work is in the owner's head, and handed out one phone call at a time, each call ending with 'is it done?'
line: The pandal ran on a list on the wall. The firm ran on the owner's calls. My Day gives each person their own list each morning, so nobody waits to be told.

title: The smallest carrier does the biggest job
image: Mushak, the small mouse at Ganesh's feet, who carries him everywhere without being asked twice.
scene: A follow-up to a client was due this morning. It was in the owner's head, the owner was in a meeting, and it went out at 7 pm with an apology.
line: The follow-up lived in the owner's head and the owner was in a meeting. It went out at 7 pm with an apology. The reminder desk carries it out at 10 am without being asked.

title: Diwali cleaning: the tray of open questions
image: The whole house turned out before Diwali: the top of the cupboard, the drawer nobody opens, the pile behind the door.
scene: Behind the owner's door is a pile of questions the team asked and never got an answer to: can we give this client credit, which vendor for the new part, is Saturday a holiday. Each one is a job standing still.
line: A pile of small questions waited behind the owner's door. Each one was a job standing still. The question tray puts them in one place, and the owner clears it once a day.

title: The new book opens; the old dues follow
image: The new account books, marked and opened on Diwali night for the first entry of the year.
scene: The new ledger opens clean. The vendor who was promised payment on the 10th and the client who owes from August both carry into it, and the owner is the only one who remembers both.
line: The new book opened clean, but the old dues came in with it, held in the owner's memory. Vendors and payments lists who is owed what and when, so the owner stops being the ledger.

title: Twenty diyas, and the one that is out
image: A row of diyas along the parapet. Nineteen burn. The eye goes straight to the one that has gone out.
scene: Twenty jobs are running. Nineteen are on time. The owner does not need to look at nineteen; the owner needs the one that has slipped, before the client calls to ask 'is it done?'
line: Twenty jobs running and the owner checked all twenty by phone. The one that slipped still got found by the client first. The owner's screen shows only the lamp that is out.

title: The sweet box went. Did the call?
image: Stacks of sweet boxes with the firm's sticker, going out to clients and vendors by the dozen.
scene: The boxes went to every client. Two of them are prospects the owner has been meaning to call since September. The box arrived; the call did not.
line: The box reached the prospect; the call never did. The season's goodwill went without a follow-up. The marketing tracker lists every contact, the last touch and the next one.

title: The same rangoli, drawn fresh each year
image: The rangoli at the door, drawn from the same dotted pattern every year, finished in an hour because nobody starts from nothing.
scene: Every quote the firm sends is typed fresh. Every job sheet is drawn from memory. The one person who knows the format is on leave this week.
line: Every quote was typed from nothing, and the format lived with one person. One leave stalled the week. The template library keeps the pattern, so the team draws from the dots.

title: One lamp lights the next
image: One diya lit from another, down the whole row, and the first loses nothing by it.
scene: The senior operator knows the machine by sound. The new one learns by standing next to him for a year, if he stays a year. Nobody has written down what the senior knows.
line: The senior knew it by sound; the junior learned by standing next to him. When the senior left, the knowledge left with him. The academy writes it down and teaches it in lessons.

title: Five days of shutters, then Monday
image: The shutter down for the Diwali week, the lock, the garland over it, the street quiet.
scene: The firm reopens on the Monday after Diwali. Who checks the stock, who calls the clients back, who clears the dispatch backlog: it all restarts from the owner's first phone call.
line: The shutter went up on Monday and the whole firm waited for the owner's first call. The week lost its morning. Routines are already on the sheet for the first working day, with a name against each.

title: Two orders, mixed like Holi colours
image: Gulal in every colour on one tray; once mixed, red and green never separate again.
scene: Two orders, two clients, one dispatch bay. The cartons went out mixed, and the owner found out when the first client called.
line: Two orders went out mixed and the client found out first. A day of unpacking and apology. The step-by-step job flow keeps each order in its own lane, step by step, name by name.

title: What burns the night before Holi
image: The Holika bonfire the night before: the old wood, the dry leaves, the things nobody wants to carry into the new season.
scene: The owner's notebook carries one-off jobs from months ago: fix the gate, call the insurer, get the sign repainted. None has a date, so none gets done.
line: The notebook carried months of small jobs with no date. None got done, and the owner carried them all. One-off tasks give each a name and a day, and the notebook is cleared by the morning.

title: Every hand that touched the kurta
image: The white kurta at the end of the day, marked by every hand that greeted it, each colour a different person.
scene: The owner knows which operator can run which machine, roughly. When one is on leave, the owner finds out at 9 am who else can do it, by asking around.
line: One operator on leave and the owner spent the morning asking who else could run the machine. The skill chart shows every person's colours, so the gap is filled before 9 am.

title: Stock needs only three colours
image: A tray of gulal in a dozen shades; the stock sheet needs only three.
scene: The storekeeper knows the stock, roughly. The owner asks every evening and gets a number from memory. The one part that ran out this week was nobody's colour.
line: The part ran out and the line stopped for a day, because stock lived in one person's memory. The stock colour sheet turns amber early, and someone reorders before red.

title: Holi is played face to face
image: Gulal applied gently to a cheek, a hug, a sweet; nobody plays Holi by message.
scene: The owner follows up with the team all week by message. The week's real problems are never said on a message; they come out when people sit across a table.
line: A week of follow-up by message and the real problem never came up. It came out on Friday, late. One sit-down a week, with the list open, is where it would have come out on Monday.

title: The pichkari reaches across the courtyard
image: The pichkari: the only way to reach the one standing across the courtyard, out of arm's reach.
scene: The CA, the transporter, the printer. They are outside the firm, outside the owner's reach, and every one of them is chased by the owner personally.
line: Three partners outside the firm, all chased by the owner personally. Each chase cost a call, a wait and a repeat. Partner follow-up reaches them on a date, and the owner sees who has replied.

title: The colour that stays for days
image: The gulal that will not wash off: three days later the pink is still on the hands.
scene: The new joiner's first week: shown the desk, shown the machine, told the rules in passing. By the second week most of it has washed off.
line: The new joiner was shown everything in passing, and a week later most of it was gone. The onboarding checklist makes week one stay: every step listed, ticked and seen.

title: Ten heads, ten follow-ups
image: Ravana's ten heads on the effigy in the ground, each one looking a different way.
scene: The owner has ten follow-ups open at once: the client, the vendor, the bank, the transporter, the site. Every one of them is looking the owner's way.
line: Ten follow-ups open, each chased from the owner's phone, each slipping while the others got attention. The reminder desk sends each one on its day, and the owner watches the ten from one place.

title: The tools are cleaned, garlanded and counted
image: Ayudha Puja: the lathe, the ledger, the vehicle, each cleaned, garlanded and given its day of respect.
scene: On Ayudha Puja every machine gets a garland. The rest of the year nobody knows when the compressor was last serviced, or which laptop went home with whom.
line: Every machine got its garland once a year, and the compressor failed in the season because nobody held its service date. The assets register holds every tool, its keeper and its next date.

title: A bridge built one stone at a time
image: The bridge to Lanka, built stone by stone, each one carried and set by a named hand.
scene: The firm's biggest job this year is three months long. It is one line on the owner's board: 'in progress'. Nobody can say which stone is being laid this week.
line: A three-month job read as one line, 'in progress', for ten weeks. Nobody could say which part was late. Project milestones show the bridge stone by stone, each with a hand and a date.

title: Every actor knows the night and the part
image: The Ramlila, staged by the whole town over ten nights; every player knows which night and which scene is theirs.
scene: In the Ramlila nobody asks the director what to do tonight. In the firm every person asks the owner what to do this morning.
line: A whole town stages ten nights without asking the director. A firm of thirty people asked the owner every morning. My Day hands each person their part before the day starts.

title: The day learning begins
image: Vijayadashami, the day children are set down to learn their first letters, because it is the right day to begin.
scene: The firm has no day for learning. The new operator learns the machine when there is a lull, which is never. The mistakes teach him instead, at the client's cost.
line: The new operator learned from his mistakes because there was never a lull to teach him. The client paid for the lessons. The academy makes a day for learning, with a lesson written for each job.

title: The bow was the test
image: The great bow in the court: not the one who spoke best, but the one who could lift and string it.
scene: The owner hired the manager who interviewed best. Three months in, nobody has seen him lift the work. The team already knows what the owner is still finding out.
line: The best interview got the job, and three months later the work was still unlifted. Hiring with a work test sets the bow on the table before the offer, and the hand shows itself.

title: The kite is two people
image: One flies the kite, one holds the spool, and the thread between them is the whole game.
scene: The quote goes from sales to the engineer to pricing to the owner for sign-off. At each hand-off the thread goes slack, and the quote that should take a day takes a week.
line: A quote passed through four hands and took a week, because every hand-off went slack. The step-by-step job flow keeps the thread taut: each step passes to a name, the same day.

title: A cut kite belongs to nobody
image: The thread is cut, the kite drifts, and the children run after it because now it belongs to whoever catches it.
scene: 'Someone should call the insurer about the godown.' Said in a meeting, agreed by all, owned by none. Two months later it is still drifting.
line: A task agreed by everyone and owned by nobody drifted for two months. One-off tasks catch it as it is said: one name, one date, one line.

title: Take the sweet, speak sweetly
image: Til-gul pressed into the palm with the old words: take this sweet and speak sweetly.
scene: The owner's weekly review is a shouting match about what slipped. The team dreads it, the owner dreads it, and the next week slips the same way.
line: The weekly review was a shouting match about what slipped, and the next week slipped the same way. One sit-down a week, with the score already on the table, leaves the shouting out.

title: The day the direction changes
image: Sankranti marks the sun turning north; the whole calendar knows the day the direction changed.
scene: The owner decided in October to stop taking small orders. The sales person who was on leave that week is still quoting them in January.
line: The direction changed in October and one person never heard. He quoted the old way for three months. The change record marks the day it turned, where everyone reads it.

title: The flyer asks, the holder answers
image: The flyer calls for slack, the one holding the spool gives it, and the kite climbs.
scene: The engineer needs a yes on a material substitution. He asks the owner by message at 11 am. The owner reads it at 6 pm. The job waited all day for one word.
line: A job waited all day for one word from the owner. The question tray holds the ask where the owner clears it at a fixed hour, and the kite climbs.

title: From the rooftop you see every kite
image: From the rooftop the whole sky is visible: every kite, whose it is, which one is in trouble.
scene: The owner sees the business from the ground: one phone call at a time, one job at a time. Nobody sees the whole sky.
line: The owner saw the business one phone call at a time and never the whole sky. The owner's screen is the rooftop: every job, who holds it, which one is dipping.

title: A promise with a date on it
image: The rakhi is tied with a promise, and the promise is remembered because it was made in front of everyone.
scene: 'You will have it by the 20th.' Said to the client on the phone, by the owner, from the car. Nobody in the firm heard it, so nobody is working to the 20th.
line: A delivery was promised from the car and nobody in the firm heard it. The 20th came and went. One-off tasks write the promise down with its date, the minute it is made.

title: The rakhi is in the courier's hands
image: The rakhi posted a week early, tracked every day, because it has to reach before the day.
scene: The client's sample is with the courier. The courier has not updated. The owner calls the courier, then the client, then the courier again.
line: The sample sat with the courier and the owner chased both ends. Partner follow-up holds the courier's promise with a date, and the chase goes out without the owner.

title: Tied once, holds all year
image: The rakhi tied in August and still on the wrist in March, holding without anyone touching it.
scene: The Monday stock check happens when the owner remembers to ask. Some Mondays the owner is travelling. Those are the Mondays the stock runs out.
line: The stock check happened only when the owner asked, and the owner was not always there. Routines are tied once and hold all year, each Monday, with a name on them.

title: What protects the firm before the signature
image: Raksha, protection: the thread is small and the promise behind it is the whole point.
scene: The order was signed without the PO number, the drawing version or the client's GST on file. Three weeks later the invoice bounces for want of a document.
line: The order was signed with a document missing and the invoice bounced three weeks later. The document checklist stands before the signature, so nothing is missing after it.

title: The thali is ready before he sits down
image: The thali laid out first: the rakhi, the sweet, the lamp, the rice. Then the brother is called.
scene: The new joiner arrived on Monday. No desk, no login, no one assigned to show her round. Her first day was spent waiting; her first impression was made.
line: The new joiner's first day was spent waiting for a desk and a login. The onboarding checklist lays the thali before she is called: every item ready, every name assigned.

title: The thread first, the gift after
image: The sister ties the thread; the brother gives the gift. Both sides of the exchange on the same day.
scene: The vendor delivered on time. The payment, promised in thirty days, went out in sixty, because the owner approves payments when the owner remembers.
line: The vendor delivered on the day; the payment went out a month late because approval waited on memory. Vendors and payments puts the gift on the same calendar as the thread.

title: Nine nights, nine days, one score
image: Nine nights, each with its own colour, its own form, its own place in the sequence; the ninth is never forgotten.
scene: The owner says, 'By next Friday, this.' Nine working days. Nobody breaks it into days, so the work happens on day eight and nine.
line: Nine days were given and the work happened on the last two. The weekly score shows each day's part done or slipped, so the ninth night is not where it all lands.

title: Two hundred people, one circle, no collisions
image: The garba circle: hundreds of people moving in time, nobody colliding, because the step is shared and the beat is known.
scene: Every morning the same things must happen: open the floor, check the mail, count the cash, call the overdue list. Each one happens if someone remembers. Collisions and gaps all day.
line: The morning's standing work happened when someone remembered, and the gaps showed by noon. Routines give the circle its step: the same things, the same time, a name on each.

title: Two sticks meet on the beat
image: Dandiya: two sticks, two people, and they meet on the beat or the line breaks.
scene: The firm's CA needs the figures by the 10th; the firm needs the return filed by the 20th. Each month one side misses the beat and the owner is the one who gets the notice.
line: The CA and the firm missed each other's beat and the owner got the notice. Partner follow-up sets the date on both sticks, and the owner sees when one is late.

title: Everyone knew today's colour without asking
image: Nine colours for nine days; the whole city shows up in the right one without a single reminder.
scene: A city of millions knew to wear yellow today. A team of twenty asked the owner what to do this morning.
line: A whole city knew the day's colour without being told. The team asked the owner for the day's work. My Day hands out the colour before the morning starts.

title: Sown on day one, measured on day nine
image: The jawara: barley sown in a clay pot on the first night and grown tall by the ninth, measured against the year before.
scene: The owner hired two trainees in June. By November nobody can say what either can now do on their own, so the owner still does the work.
line: Two trainees grew for five months and nobody measured what they could now do, so the owner still did it. The skill chart shows the growth by name, step by step.

title: Each doll on its own step
image: The golu: dolls set out on nine steps, each on its step, nothing on the floor.
scene: The firm's job board shows jobs in two states: 'going on' and 'done'. Between them is where everything is lost.
line: Every job was 'going on' until it was 'done', and the middle was where it got lost. Project milestones set each job on its step, so the owner sees which step is empty.

title: The metal bought today goes on the register
image: Dhanteras: the day the house buys metal, a new vessel or a coin, and it is counted into the house.
scene: The firm bought a compressor in March, two laptops in June, a vehicle last year. Nobody can say where the compressor's warranty card is or whose laptop came back.
line: The firm bought metal all year and nobody could say where each piece was or when it was due for service. The assets register counts everything in on the day it is bought.

title: The lamp that stands guard all night
image: The Dhanteras lamp set outside the door at dusk, kept burning through the night, watching while the house sleeps.
scene: The follow-up to the bank is due tomorrow at 10. The owner will remember it at 10:40, in another meeting.
line: The follow-up was due at 10 and remembered at 10:40, in another meeting. The reminder desk stands at the door all night and goes out at 10.

title: Dhanvantari, and the health of the firm
image: Dhanteras is also Dhanvantari's day, the day of health; wealth begins with a body that works.
scene: The owner knows the firm's revenue to the rupee and its health not at all: how much slipped this week, how much was chased, how many jobs are late.
line: The owner knew the revenue to the rupee and the health not at all. Every Friday the weekly score reads the firm's pulse: done, slipped, late, by name.

title: Weighed before it is bought
image: The silver weighed on the shop's scale before a rupee changes hands; nothing bought by guess.
scene: The storekeeper says 'enough' when asked about stock. 'Enough' ran out on Wednesday.
line: Stock was 'enough' until it was gone on Wednesday. The stock colour sheet weighs it every day: green, amber, red, and a reorder before red.

title: Three shops, then the price is written
image: Before buying, the family visits three shops and the rate is written on a slip before the choice is made.
scene: The vendor's rate was agreed on a call. The invoice came in higher. Nobody can find what was agreed, so the owner pays it.
line: The rate was agreed on a call and the invoice came in higher. The owner paid the difference for want of a slip. Vendors and payments writes the rate before the order, and the invoice is checked against it.

title: One more vessel in the kitchen each year
image: Every Dhanteras adds one vessel to the kitchen; over the years the shelf tells the family's story.
scene: Every year the team should add one skill a person: a second machine, a second language, the dispatch module. Nobody tracks it, so nobody adds it.
line: A year passed and nobody on the team had added a skill, because nobody was tracking it. The skill chart adds one vessel a year, by name, and the shelf fills.

title: The year-end stock count
image: The last week of December: shutters half down, the stock count on clipboards, every shelf touched once.
scene: The stock is counted once a year, in the last week, and the count never matches the book. The difference is the year's leakage, discovered too late to fix.
line: The stock was counted once a year and never matched the book. The stock colour sheet counts the moving items every week, so December's count is a formality.

title: The quiet week is training week
image: The week between Christmas and New Year: clients away, phones quiet, the floor half full.
scene: The quietest week of the year is spent waiting for it to end. The training nobody had time for in October has time now.
line: The quietest week of the year passed waiting for January. The academy uses it: a lesson a day, written for each job, so the new year starts with a trained floor.

title: The list, checked twice before dispatch
image: The season's gift lists on the counter, every name ticked twice before the parcel goes.
scene: The year's last dispatch went without the test certificate. The client's gate refused it on the 2nd of January, and the year began with a return.
line: The year's last dispatch went without one certificate and came back on the 2nd. The document checklist is checked twice at the bay, before the parcel goes.

title: Half the floor is on leave
image: The December leave roster on the wall: half the names crossed out for the last fortnight.
scene: Half the team is on leave and the other half does not know which of the absent team's jobs are now theirs. The owner is doing the re-assignment by phone.
line: Half the team was away and the other half did not know what was now theirs. My Day moves the list to whoever is in, each morning, without the owner's phone.

title: Ordered in November, collected on the 24th
image: The cake order placed at the bakery in November, slip in the drawer, collected on the 24th.
scene: The vendor's part was ordered in November for a January job. Nobody followed up in December. On the 2nd it is not ready.
line: The part was ordered in November and nobody chased it in December, so January started late. Partner follow-up holds the vendor's date and asks in between.

title: The last sit-down of the year
image: The last working Friday: the office half dark, the year's folders stacked, a cup of tea and a long look back.
scene: The year's review is a feeling: it felt busy, it felt hard. Nobody can say what slipped most or who carried the most.
line: The year's review was a feeling, because the weeks were never reviewed. One sit-down a week, fifty-two of them, makes the last Friday a reading, not a guess.

title: The resolution, scored every Friday
image: The new year resolution written on the first page of the new diary, in a careful hand.
scene: 'This year, no job goes late.' Said every January. By March nobody remembers, because nothing measured it week by week.
line: The January resolution was forgotten by March, because nothing scored it. The weekly score reads it out every Friday: done, slipped, late, by name.

title: The first Monday of the year
image: The first Monday: new diary, clean desk, the whole team waiting to be told where to start.
scene: The first Monday of the year begins with the whole team looking at the owner. The year's first hour is spent handing out work by voice.
line: The year's first hour went on handing out work by voice. My Day puts each person's Monday list in front of them before they sit down.

title: Last year's decisions, in this year's diary
image: The new diary's first page, blank; last year's diary closed and put away with everything decided in it.
scene: Last year the owner decided to stop giving credit beyond thirty days. It was in last year's diary. The new sales person has never seen it.
line: Last year's decision was in last year's diary, and this year's hire never saw it. The change record carries every decision across the first page, dated and readable.

title: Your calendar is on their wall
image: The printed calendar with the firm's name, hung on client walls in the first week of January.
scene: The calendar went to every client and prospect. It will hang there all year. The follow-up call to the ten who were warm in December is in nobody's diary.
line: The calendar reached every wall; the follow-up reached none. The marketing tracker lists each contact, the last touch and the next, so January's warmth is not wasted.

title: Resolutions lapse. Routines do not.
image: The gym membership bought on the 1st and quiet by the 20th of February; everyone knows the shape of it.
scene: The daily cash count, the Monday stock check, the Friday review: each started in January with resolve and lapsed when the owner got busy.
line: The January routines lapsed in February when the owner got busy. Routines do not run on resolve; they sit on the sheet with a name and a day, and ask to be ticked.

title: This year we hire a manager
image: The January plan on the whiteboard, and at the top of it: hire a manager.
scene: Every January the owner resolves to hire a manager. Every year the interviews go well and the hire does not. Nobody saw the candidate work before the offer.
line: Every January's hire interviewed well and worked badly, because nobody saw the work first. Hiring with a work test puts one afternoon of real work before the offer.

title: The pot boils over, and everyone watches
image: The whole family around the pot at dawn, waiting for the milk to rise and spill over the rim.
scene: In season the enquiries boil over: calls, messages, walk-ins. Each one is answered if someone is free. The ones from the first week are already cold.
line: Enquiries boiled over in season and the first week's went cold while the rest were answered. The marketing tracker catches each as it rises, with a next step and a date.

title: The kolam, drawn fresh every dawn
image: The kolam at the doorstep, drawn before sunrise from the same grid of dots, every single morning.
scene: The morning opening: lights, cash, mail, the overdue list. It is done well on the days the senior person is in, and not at all on the others.
line: The morning opening depended on who was in, and some mornings it did not happen. Routines are the dots on the step: the same pattern, drawn fresh by name, every dawn.

title: What leaves the house on Bhogi
image: Bhogi: the old things carried out of the house, the broken chair, the worn mat, the year's clutter, before the new begins.
scene: The firm has scrapped two machines, sold a vehicle and lent a laptop this year. The register, if there is one, still lists all of them as present.
line: Two machines were scrapped and the register still showed them, so the insurer and the auditor both asked. The assets register records what went out on Bhogi, and what stayed.

title: The ones who pull the load
image: Mattu Pongal: the cattle washed, horns painted, garlanded and thanked for the year's pulling.
scene: The team is thanked once a year, at the party. The rest of the year the owner sees only what slipped, never what was carried.
line: The team was seen once a year and chased the other fifty-one weeks. The weekly score shows what each person carried, every Friday, beside what slipped.

title: Cut, bundled, loaded, sent
image: The sugarcane harvest: cut in the field, tied in bundles, loaded on the cart, sent to the mandi, each by a different pair of hands.
scene: An order goes from production to packing to the invoice to the transporter. Four hands, and the owner is the thread between every pair.
line: Four hands on every order and the owner was the thread between each pair. The step-by-step job flow ties the hand-off: cut, bundled, loaded, sent, each to a name.

title: A new pot, the same recipe
image: A new clay pot bought every year for the Pongal rice; the recipe has not changed in a generation.
scene: Every new job sheet, every quote, every delivery note is made new by whoever is doing it that day. The recipe lives in people, not on paper.
line: Every quote was made new by whoever was free, and no two matched. The template library keeps the recipe on paper, so each new pot is filled the same way.

title: The pookalam grows a ring a day
image: The pookalam at the doorstep: one ring of flowers on day one, a ring added each day, complete on the tenth.
scene: The client's fit-out is a ten-week job. The owner sees it as one job, not ten rings. Week six is where it slips and nobody notices until week nine.
line: A ten-week job slipped in week six and nobody saw until week nine. Project milestones add a ring a day: each week's part named, dated, visible.

title: Every dish in its place on the leaf
image: The sadya on the banana leaf: salt at the top left, pickle beside it, every dish in its fixed place, the same in every house.
scene: The firm's delivery challan is laid out differently by each person who makes it. The client's gate keeper rejects the one that looks unfamiliar.
line: Each delivery note was laid out by whoever made it, and the client's gate rejected the odd one. The template library sets the leaf: every item in its place, every time.

title: A hundred oars, one beat
image: The vallam kali: a hundred rowers in a boat, every oar lifting on the same beat, each man in his own seat.
scene: The dispatch team has eight people. On a busy day three are doing the same thing and nobody is loading the second vehicle.
line: Eight people on dispatch and three doing one job while the second vehicle stood empty. My Day gives each rower a seat and a stroke before the boat leaves.

title: The king comes to see his people
image: Mahabali's annual visit: the king returns once a year to see that his people are well, and the house is made ready for him.
scene: The owner walks the floor when the owner is in town. The rest of the time the floor is a phone call away, and the phone only carries what someone chooses to say.
line: The owner saw the floor only when in town, and the phone carried only what people chose to say. The owner's screen shows the whole house every morning, from anywhere.

title: New clothes for everyone, in the right size
image: The Onakkodi: new clothes for every member of the house, bought in advance, in each one's size.
scene: The new hire's kit should have been ready: uniform, ID, login, the three forms, a person to sit with. It was assembled over her first week, one item a day.
line: The new hire's kit arrived one item a day across her first week. The onboarding checklist buys every size in advance, with a name against each item.

title: The rope is tested before anyone swings
image: The Onam swing tied to the mango tree, and an uncle pulling hard on the rope before any child climbs on.
scene: The new supervisor was hired on his word. The first time the rope was tested was in the season, with the client watching.
line: The supervisor's rope was first tested in season, with the client watching. Hiring with a work test pulls on it before the offer, with no one on the swing.

title: Weighed at the mandi, paid on the day
image: The harvest at the mandi: weighed on the scale, the slip written, the payment made against the slip.
scene: The firm's vendors deliver, the goods are weighed in, and the payment waits on the owner's signature. Some wait a week, some two months, and the good vendors stop answering.
line: The good vendors stopped answering because their slips waited on the owner's signature for two months. Vendors and payments lists every slip with its due day, and the owner signs in one sitting.

title: The sickle is sharpened before the harvest
image: The sickle sharpened in the week before Baisakhi, not in the field with the crop standing.
scene: The firm's season starts in April. The two new operators will learn the machine in April, in the season, at the pace of the mistakes they make.
line: The new operators learned in the season, at the cost of the season's mistakes. The academy sharpens the sickle in March: a lesson for each job, before the crop is standing.

title: The dhol sets the beat for the field
image: The dhol at the centre of the bhangra; everybody dances to the one beat, and nobody needs telling.
scene: The week has no beat. It starts when the owner arrives and ends when the owner stops calling. Nobody knows when the week is reviewed, so nothing is ready for it.
line: The week had no beat, so nothing was ready when the owner asked. One sit-down a week, same day, same hour, is the dhol: the whole floor works to it.

title: The arhtiya stands between you and the buyer
image: The arhtiya at the mandi, the commission agent between farmer and buyer, through whom every sale and every payment passes.
scene: The firm sells through two agents and ships through three transporters. Every one of them is followed up by the owner, from memory, on the phone.
line: Five partners outside the firm, each followed up from the owner's memory, each slipping when the owner was busy. Partner follow-up holds every agent's promise with a date.

title: The first cut shows the hand
image: The first sickle stroke of the harvest: a morning in the field shows more than a month of talk.
scene: The owner has interviewed six people for the dispatch role. All six spoke well. Nobody has seen any of them pack a carton.
line: Six candidates spoke well and none had packed a carton. Hiring with a work test gives each one a morning in the field, and the first cut shows the hand.

title: Everyone you met at the mela
image: The Baisakhi mela: the whole district in one ground, and a hundred handshakes before noon.
scene: The owner came back from the trade fair with a pocket of cards. Three were good. By the next month the cards are in a drawer and the three are cold.
line: A pocket of cards from the fair went into a drawer, and the three good ones went cold. The marketing tracker lists each handshake with a next step and a date.

title: The gudi, raised where the street sees
image: The gudi at the window: the bamboo, the silk, the garland, the upturned pot, raised high so the whole street sees it.
scene: The firm's week ends with the owner knowing how it went. Nobody else does. The team finds out which jobs slipped when the owner is angry about them.
line: Only the owner knew how the week went, and the team found out when the owner was angry. The weekly score is raised at the window every Friday, where the whole floor can see it.

title: Neem and jaggery, in the same mouthful
image: Neem leaves and jaggery eaten together on the first morning of the year: the bitter and the sweet in one mouthful.
scene: The owner's review covers only the bitter: what slipped, who was late. The sweet is never said, so the team hears only the neem.
line: The weekly review served only the neem, and the team stopped listening. One sit-down a week puts both on the table: what was carried, what slipped, in the same mouthful.

title: The year's dates, read on the first day
image: The new panchang opened on Gudi Padwa: every date of the year already set down, from the first day.
scene: The GST date, the salary day, the stock count, the client's monthly review: each comes as a surprise, every month, to someone.
line: The month's fixed dates arrived as surprises, every month, to someone. Routines are the panchang: every standing date set down on the first day, with a name beside it.

title: Begin one thing on the right day
image: Gudi Padwa is the day for beginning: a venture, a purchase, a first step, chosen because the day is right.
scene: The owner wants everything fixed at once: dispatch, quotes, payments, hiring. So nothing starts. The right day has passed four times.
line: Everything was to be fixed at once, so nothing began. The step-by-step job flow starts with one process, the one that costs the most chasing, on one chosen day.

title: Every leaf on the string before it hangs
image: The mango-leaf toran at the door, strung leaf by leaf, checked along its length before it goes up.
scene: The tender was submitted with one certificate missing from the set. It was found at the opening, by the other side.
line: The tender went out one leaf short, and the other side found it at the opening. The document checklist strings every leaf before it hangs at the door.

title: Set the night before, calm in the morning
image: The shrikhand hung in muslin the night before Gudi Padwa, so the morning has nothing to do but serve.
scene: The 10 am follow-up to the client is prepared at 9:55, by the owner, between two other calls.
line: The 10 am follow-up was prepared at 9:55 between two calls. The reminder desk sets it the night before, and the morning only serves.

title: Six tastes in one spoon
image: Ugadi pachadi: neem, jaggery, tamarind, salt, chilli, raw mango; the whole year's six tastes in one spoon.
scene: The owner's view of the firm is one taste at a time: today a late job, tomorrow an unpaid invoice, the next day a missing part. Never the whole spoon.
line: The owner tasted the firm one problem at a time and never the whole bowl. The owner's screen is the pachadi: jobs, payments, stock, people, in one spoon each morning.

title: The year read aloud, then the week
image: Panchanga sravanam: the new year's almanac read aloud to the gathered family, so everyone hears the same year.
scene: The owner knows what this week holds. The team hears it in pieces, by phone, during the week, after it has already started.
line: The week was known to the owner and heard by the team in pieces, after it started. My Day reads the day aloud to each person before it begins.

title: A fresh coat, the same house
image: The house whitewashed before Ugadi: same walls, same rooms, a fresh coat so the year begins clean.
scene: The firm's quote format has not been touched in years, and each sales person has their own copy with their own changes. No two quotes look like one firm.
line: No two quotes looked like one firm, because each person kept their own copy. The template library gives the house its fresh coat once a year, and one copy to everyone.

title: New clothes, ready before the day
image: New clothes for every member of the house, bought and set out before Ugadi morning.
scene: The new joiner's ID, login, uniform and first-day guide should be ready before she arrives. They were ready on Thursday. She started Monday.
line: The new joiner's kit was ready on Thursday; she started Monday. The onboarding checklist lays out every item before the morning, with a name against each.

title: What last year decided, on this year's page
image: The first page of the new year, and the year that closed behind it, full of what was decided and by whom.
scene: The firm changed its credit terms, its vendor for packaging and its dispatch cut-off last year. Each change lives with the person who heard it first.
line: Three changes last year, each living with whoever heard it first. The change record carries each decision onto the new year's page, dated and read by all.

title: The bitter taste, taken first
image: In the pachadi the neem is tasted first and deliberately; the year's bitterness is not hidden at the bottom.
scene: The team's hard questions, about a client who does not pay or a machine that keeps failing, are saved for the owner's good mood. The good mood is rare, so the questions wait.
line: The hard questions waited for the owner's good mood, and the good mood was rare. The question tray takes the bitter first: every question in one place, cleared once a day.
